open_decision: The laws do not fix the order of the new rows after the old registry, and they do not forbid repeated identical new rows.
input: Config: locked = fun _ => false, enable = false. Starter list: [{id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:true}, {id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:true}]. Registry: [].
result_a: ref (starter order): [{id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:false}, {id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:false}]
result_b: Same design with the new rows reversed: [{id:2, adapter:2, model:2, enabled:false}, {id:1, adapter:1, model:1, enabled:false}]
reason: Every law talks about membership of rows, or about the old registry as a prefix. No law says in what order the new rows follow the prefix. So the reversed design passes every law and gives a different registry.
